messages:
roxanne: quick lane-level question: given the small-request burst patterns we're seeing, is it better to add a tiny-fast queue or make the admission layer return a headroom token that hints for immediate dispatch?
ben_s: tiny-fast queue seems simplest to reason about, but it fragments packing heuristics and can increase warmup misses. headroom token could let the packer decide.
jia_w: headroom tokens need strong semantics. if we return 'headroom=2' that must mean the packer reserves X tokens or the latency SLO breaks. careful.
omar_ops: ops note: any change must have per-queue kill-switch and visible cost counters. tiny-fast will spike cost unless we gate it.
adrian_r: thought: use a "burst-tax" approach: small requests can pay a small token-cost to jump the queue (probabilistic). keeps packer behavior intact unless SLOs demand it.
roxanne: interesting. burst-tax maps well to multi-tenant pricing blocks, but it's awkward for internal tenants. can we model it as 'urgency credit' instead? requesters get credits for occasional fast path.
ben_s: implementation sketch: admission returns {queue_tag, slot_token, urgency_credit_used:false}. packer uses queue_tag; if urgency_credit_used flips true we decrease credit bucket. slot_token is opaque for warmup.
jia_w: we also need to avoid stampeding warmups if many slot_tokens are issued for the same model. propose a per-model warmup debouncer keyed with a short TTL and a concurrency cap per device.
adrian_r: agree. we should emit warmup_dedupe, warmup_concurrency, and warmup_latency metrics.
omar_ops: rescue plan: if warmups cause hotspot, circuit-break the warmup path and route to legacy packer with a warn log. need a paged runbook.
roxanne: preemption idea: rather than evicting inflight batches, have the packer maintain a small expedited lane that can steal a fraction of capacity when a high-urgency token arrives. it's simpler than split/re-enqueue.
ben_s: expedited lane still affects packing but is pretested: we can reserve N microbatches per-GPU for expedited work. fewer moving parts.
jia_w: downside: reserved capacity can be underutilized. maybe make reserved capacity adaptive based on observed urgent fraction.
adrian_r: adaptive reserve + decay window sounds good. tune with simulator. we need a harness to sweep burstiness and urgent-fraction to pick defaults.
omar_ops: ops items: feature-flag per-pool, per-region kill-switch, dashboards for burst_tax_usage, urgent_queue_waits, warmup_losses, and a rollback playbook.
roxanne: agreed. action items: ben prototype admission headroom API with slot_token opaque, jia add warmup dedupe + concurrency cap, adrian build sim harness for burst-tax calibration, omar write runbook + dashboards. I'll draft RFC follow-up with these options and a recommended default (adaptive expedited lane + warmup dedupe).
adrian_r: +1. also include cost model showing when burst-tax beats reserved lanes.
ben_s: will post a light prototype this week.
roxanne: thanks all, please comment on the draft when I post it. :thumbsup:
